Normalized exponential pooling matches the adjusted exponentially weighted mean documented by [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.ewm.html). Deriving its masked recurrence: let q=exp(−softplus(b)), valid-token mask m_t∈{0,1}, and initialize S=0, Z=0. Update S_t=qS_{t−1}+m_t e_t, Z_t=qZ_{t−1}+m_t, then p_t=S_t/max(Z_t,ε). Mask padding outputs to zero. This uses O(Ld) work and O(d) streaming state; training autograd retains intermediate states. Accumulate in float32, avoid in-place updates and inverse powers q^(−t), and keep beta connected to autograd. The recurrence handles left padding directly; internal padding consumes a time step. To ignore internal padding, preserve both states whenever m_t=0. Positive beta prevents exponential growth; beta=0 gives exact uniform pooling and should be an explicit ablation.

Recommended controls, rather than established findings: compare backbone alone; backbone plus uniform pooling; fixed-decay pooling; learned-decay pooling; and last-item pooling. Cross uniform/fixed/learned pooling with identical projection and fusion modules, including identity/no-projection variants, to isolate added capacity. Compare ordinary occurrence weighting against per-prefix unique-item pooling or inverse-count weighting, keeping input histories unchanged; shuffle only the auxiliary pooling branch to preserve item counts while disrupting recency. Recency sampling is a separate training intervention, as illustrated by [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), so hold training targets and sampling fixed. Use identical initialization for shared parameters, separate RNG streams for auxiliary modules, identical batches/negatives, and pinned evaluation candidates. Report per-category and macro validation HR@10, learned half-lives ln(2)/beta, and runtime; retain preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42.
